correctness.rationale: From the actual RESULT.md blob 3c45823b, verified the three generalized-key I2 equations, positive-root quotient t=(z0/z1)^(1/k), t-sum solution z0=t^k/G, z1=1/G, z2=A/G, lambda=A^k/(B^k G), and t<->1/t symmetry. G>0 reduces to Phi_k=log a-k log(c/b)>0. H_s(u)=u coth(us) has H_s>0 for u>0, making Phi_k strictly decreasing from positive at s=0 (k>=4) to -infinity, hence unique finite positivity endpoint. Taylor expansion yields exact lambda_c and curvature coefficient B_k; independent 45-digit evaluation gives B4=14.5712087576985, B5=1.38823505199204, B6=-5.08810841405847, B7=-11.20358. Algebraic inequality gives B_k<0 for all k>=6. Continuity plus divergence at the endpoint gives a strict interior level below lambda_c and two positive-s solutions at each intermediate level, each with a distinct reciprocal partner. This proves AT LEAST four I2 boundary laws, not exactly four, for every integer k>=6; verifier samples alone are not the proof.
